info.name: ArbiPilot
info.description: Every endpoint of the ArbiPilot backend, one folder per group, in the same order as docs/api.md. Choose the Development or Production environment (top right) before sending. No token, password or key is saved in this file.

exec: pm.test('Says which environment and mode', function () {

request.description: Returns the environment, the trading mode and the version. Always 200 while the app runs.
200 when the database, Binance, the Claude API and Telegram all answer. 503 when any one fails; the body then says which one and why. The answer is reused for 15 seconds.

response.name: 503 - the database is unreachable

item.name: Login
item.description: Register once, then log in. The Login request saves both tokens into the environment by itself; every later request sends the access token automatically. Type your email and password into the environment (top right, eye icon), never into this file.

exec: pm.test('No password in the answer', function () {

request.description: Creates the owner account. Works once: after that it answers 409 for good. Uses {{email}} and {{password}} from the environment. The password needs at least 12 characters.

exec: pm.test('Tokens saved for the next requests', function () {

request.description: Checks the email and password. Returns an access token (30 minutes) and a refresh token (7 days), and saves both into the environment. Wrong passwords cause growing waits: 1 s, 2 s, 4 s ... up to 15 minutes.

response.name: 429 - waiting after wrong passwords

exec: pm.test('Tokens saved for the next requests', function () {

request.description: Swaps the refresh token for a new pair and saves it. Each refresh token works once.

response.name: 401 - token used, cancelled or expired

exec: pm.test('Tokens saved for the next requests', function () {

request.description: Changes the password while logged in. Every other session is logged out; the answer carries new tokens, saved automatically. Put the new password in the environment variable new_password first. Afterwards, copy it into the password variable.

item.name: Forgot password - send a code to Telegram

request.description: Sends a six-digit code to the owner's Telegram. It works for 10 minutes and once. The answer is the same whether or not the email exists. A new code can be asked for once a minute.

response.name: 200 - same answer in every case

request.description: Sets a new password using the code from Telegram. Replace 000000 in the body with your code (the space in the middle is optional). Five wrong codes cancel it. Afterwards, copy the new password into the password variable and log in.

response.name: 200 - password changed
400 - wrong, used or expired code

request.description: Cancels the refresh token. The access token keeps working until its 30 minutes are over.

exec: pm.test('No password in the answer', function () {

request.description: Returns the logged-in user's profile. Without a valid access token it answers 401.
Changes the display name. Send null to clear it. The email cannot be changed here.

item.name: Me - without a token (must be refused)

request.description: The same request with no token. It must answer 401: that is the proof the door is locked.

item.name: Connections
item.description: One check per outside service. Login needed. 200 means it works, 503 means it does not and "detail" says why.

exec: pm.test('The check passed (200). 503 means it failed: read "detail"', function () {

request.description: Checks Binance is reachable, the clocks agree, and every key in .env is valid and safe. On the laptop only the testnet key exists; withdrawals and the IP lock can only be checked for mainnet keys (on the server). The answer is reused for 15 seconds.

response.name: 200 - ok
response.body:
{
  "status": "ok",
  "detail": "",
  "host": "api.binance.com",
  "reachable": true,
  "clock_difference_ms": 60,
  "keys": [
    {
      "name": "testnet",
      "exchange": "testnet",
      "ok": true,
      "valid": true,
      "trading_allowed": true,
      "withdrawals_enabled": null,
      "ip_restricted": null,
      "spot_only": null,
      "maker_fee": "0.00100000",
      "taker_fee": "0.00100000",
      "detail": "the testnet has no withdrawals and no IP lock, so those two cannot be checked here"
    }
  ]
}

response.name: 503 - the check failed
response.body:
{
  "status": "failed",
  "detail": "testnet key: Binance refused the key (wrong key, a caller address the key is not locked to, or a missing permission)",
  "host": "api.binance.com",
  "reachable": true,
  "clock_difference_ms": 60,
  "keys": [
    {
      "name": "testnet",
      "exchange": "testnet",
      "ok": false,
      "valid": false,
      "trading_allowed": null,
      "withdrawals_enabled": null,
      "ip_restricted": null,
      "spot_only": null,
      "maker_fee": null,
      "taker_fee": null,
      "detail": "Binance refused the key (wrong key, a caller address the key is not locked to, or a missing permission)"
    }
  ]
}
